subject: Discovering the number of probe pairs per SNP

messages.author: bc1f4b339b21de43
messages.subject: Discovering the number of probe pairs per SNP
parts:
Hi all,

I would like to find out the number of probe pairs per SNP (unit) for a
given CDF. Is there an easy way to find this? Is it stored somewhere in
the header or elsewhere?

At the moment I am extracting the units from the CDF (using readUnits)
and merging the strands. Then I loop over the units and take the length
of the relevant part of the structure. I was hoping for an easier or
smarter way.

I am only interested in perfect match probes and only those SNPs on
chromosomes 1:22, if that helps.

Cheers,
Tim Keighley

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Discovering the number of probe pairs per SNP

On Tue, May 13, 2008 at 6:43 PM, <Tim.Ke...@csiro.au> wrote:
>
> Hi all,
>
> I would like to find out the number of probe pairs per SNP (unit) for a
> given CDF. Is there an easy way to find this? Is it stored somewhere in
> the header or elsewhere?
It is not stored in the CDF header, but in every unit of the CDF structure.

>
> At the moment I am extracting the units from the CDF (using readUnits)
> and merging the strands. Then I loop over the units and take the length
> of the relevant part of the structure. I was hoping for an easier or
> smarter way.
>
> I am only interested in perfect match probes and only those SNPs on
> chromosomes 1:22, if that helps.

In affxparser there is readCdfNbrOfCellsPerUnitGroup() that helps you, e.g.

cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType("Mapping250K_Nsp");
pathname <- getPathname(cdf);
nbrOfCellsPerUnitGroup <- readCdfNbrOfCellsPerUnitGroup(pathname,
units=2001:2005);
print(nbrOfCellsPerUnitGroup)

$`SNP_A-2062566`
C T C T
8 8 4 4

$`SNP_A-4219688`
C T C T
8 8 4 4

$`SNP_A-4219711`
A C A C
10 10 10 10

$`SNP_A-2063043`
A G A G
6 6 6 6

$`SNP_A-2063124`
C T C T
4 4 8 8

nbrOfCellsPerUnit <- sapply(nbrOfCellsPerUnitGroup, FUN=sum);
print(nbrOfCellsPerUnit)
SNP_A-2062566 SNP_A-4219688 SNP_A-4219711 SNP_A-2063043 SNP_A-2063124
24 24 40 24 24

It does not allow you to stratify on PM or MM, but for the SNP chips
the rule is that if the chip type has MMs then all SNPs have them, so
you can easily divide by two to get the number of PMs.

nbrOfPMs <- nbrOfCellsPerUnit/2; # For Mapping250K_Nsp
nbrOfPMs <- nbrOfCellsPerUnit/1; # For GenomeWideSNP_6

and finally the number of Allele (A,B) pairs:

nbrOfAllelePairs <- nbrOfPMs/2;

You can use:

gi <- getGenomeInformation(cdf);
units <- getUnitsOnChromosome(gi, 1:22);

to identify the units of interest.

Hope this helps

Henrik
